absent: Locking discipline, concurrency rules, reference counting and lifetime management for maps, programs, links and iterators.
System-call numbers, dispatch logic, privilege and capability checks, verifier semantics and helper availability.
Kernel-side implementation, allocation, eviction algorithms, error codes and errno mapping for ioctls and commands.
Zone on-disk layout, zone state transitions and device behavior beyond ioctl numbers and carrier names.
Remaining bpf_attr command views, info and query records and iterator semantics beyond the truncated load view.
ABI stability, versioning and 32-bit versus 64-bit compatibility beyond aligned 64-bit markers and name bounds.

findings.text: This lane exposes block zone management and packet-filter user interfaces through shared headers. The zone side offers report, reset, size query, count query, open, close, finish and version-two report operations. The filter side offers instruction encoding, register numbering, map and program taxonomies, command multiplexing, attachment and link taxonomies, flag bits, pseudo source markers, statistics and attribute carriers. Examples are BLKREPORTZONE for zones and BPF_MAP_CREATE for maps.

Zone control uses ioctl type 0x12. BLKREPORTZONE is read-write number 130 with report carrier. BLKRESETZONE is write-only number 131 with range carrier. BLKGETZONESZ is read-only number 132 returning unsigned 32 bits for size. BLKGETNRZONES is read-only number 133 returning unsigned 32 bits for count. BLKOPENZONE then BLKCLOSEZONE then BLKFINISHZONE are write-only numbers 134 through 136 with range carrier for lifecycle transitions. BLKREPORTZONEV2 is read-write number 142 with report carrier for the newer report variant. Carriers are blk_zone_report and blk_zone_range and plain 32-bit unsigned.

BPF_JMP32 denotes 32-bit jump with value 0x06. BPF_ALU64 denotes 64-bit ALU with value 0x07. BPF_DW denotes double word with value 0x18. BPF_MEMSX denotes sign-extending load with value 0x80. BPF_ATOMIC denotes atomic memory operations with value 0xc0. BPF_XADD is the legacy exclusive-add alias for the same value. BPF_MOV denotes register move with value 0xb0. BPF_ARSH denotes sign-extending shift with value 0xc0 in its field. BPF_END denotes endian conversion with base 0xd0. BPF_TO_LE is 0x00 for little endian and BPF_TO_BE is 0x08 for big endian, with BPF_FROM_LE and BPF_FROM_BE aliasing the respective to-direction values.

Jump tests distinguish signedness. BPF_JNE means not-equal with value 0x50. BPF_JLT means unsigned less with 0xa0. BPF_JLE means unsigned less-or-equal with 0xb0. BPF_JSGT means signed greater with 0x60. BPF_JSGE means signed greater-or-equal with 0x70. BPF_JSLT means signed less with 0xc0. BPF_JSLE means signed less-or-equal with 0xd0. BPF_JCOND marks conditional pseudo jumps with 0xe0. BPF_CALL marks helper invocation with 0x80 and BPF_EXIT marks program return with 0x90. BPF_FETCH is value 0x01 used only as a combiner bit. BPF_XCHG combines 0xe0 with that bit for atomic exchange and BPF_CMPXCHG combines 0xf0 with that bit for compare exchange. Acquire load uses 0x100 under BPF_LOAD_ACQ and release store uses 0x110 under BPF_STORE_REL. The pseudo-jump enumeration defines BPF_MAY_GOTO as zero.

The guard macro _UAPI__LINUX_BPF_H__ marks single inclusion of the user API. Registers are numbered contiguously from zero for BPF_REG_0 through ten for BPF_REG_10 with a trailing sentinel __MAX_BPF_REG and a public limit MAX_BPF_REG equal to that sentinel. The instruction carrier named bpf_insn holds an eight-bit operation code, then destination and source selectors packed as four bits each with destination first, then a signed sixteen-bit offset, then a signed thirty-two-bit immediate.

The fixed key named bpf_lpm_trie_key carries a 32-bit prefix length followed by a zero-length tail for arbitrary bytes, with guidance up to 32 for IPv4 and 128 for IPv6. The header named bpf_lpm_trie_key_hdr carries only the length. The flexible key named bpf_lpm_trie_key_u8 overlays length with a header through a union and then a flexible byte tail. The storage key named bpf_cgroup_storage_key combines a 64-bit cgroup inode identifier with a 32-bit attachment type drawn from the attach taxonomy.

Cgroup iteration defines a traversal selector with six modes. Unspecified starts the enumeration. Single mode visits one object. Preorder and postorder walk below the start including the start with different visit timing. Upward mode walks ancestors. Children mode visits only immediate children excluding the parent, unlike descendant modes which include the start. Selector is bpf_cgroup_iter_order with members for unspecified and single and preorder and postorder and upward and immediate children in increasing order from zero.

Link creation parameters for iterators form a discriminated carrier named bpf_iter_link_info with three variants. The map variant carries only a map descriptor. The cgroup variant carries an order selector plus a descriptor plus a 64-bit identifier, with a rule that at most one of descriptor and identifier may be nonzero and zero for both means start at the default version-two root, while version-one walks should always set the descriptor explicitly. The task variant carries thread identifier plus process identifier plus process descriptor as three 32-bit values.

The multiplexed control interface defines a command taxonomy covering map lifecycle and element access, program loading, object pinning and retrieval, attachment and detachment, test execution with a run alias, identifier iteration and lookup by identifier, info retrieval, query, raw tracepoint opening, type-format loading and lookup, task descriptor query, lookup-and-delete, freeze, batched lookup and update and delete, link lifecycle, statistics enablement, iterator creation, map binding, token creation, stream read and struct-ops association. Examples include BPF_MAP_CREATE for creation and BPF_PROG_LOAD for loading and BPF_LINK_CREATE for linking and BPF_ITER_CREATE for iteration and BPF_TOKEN_CREATE for delegation, bounded by a max marker with a high bit-sixteen marker for common attributes.

Map taxonomy spans generic hash, fixed array, program array, perf array, per-CPU hash and array, stack trace, cgroup array, least-recently-used hash and per-CPU hash, longest-prefix trie, nested maps of arrays and hashes, device and socket and CPU and transmit and socket-hash families, reuse-port arrays, queue and stack, socket and device-hash and struct-ops and ring and inode and task and bloom and user-ring and cgroup-local and arena and instruction-array and resizable-hash families. Bounds are BPF_MAP_TYPE_UNSPEC at the start and __MAX_BPF_MAP_TYPE at the end, with BPF_MAP_TYPE_CGROUP_STORAGE aliasing its deprecated predecessor and the per-CPU cgroup variant aliasing its own deprecated predecessor.

Program taxonomy covers socket filtering, probes, traffic-control classifier and action, tracepoints, packet data path, perf events, cgroup socket and device and address and sysctl and socket-option hooks, tunnel stages, socket operations and messaging and reuse-port and lookup, infrared, flow dissection, writable tracepoints, tracing and struct-ops and extension and security-module and netfilter and syscall-capable programs. Attachment taxonomy refines hook points for network, tracing, security and device paths. Link taxonomy enumerates persistent handles from raw tracepoint through tracing, cgroup, iterator, namespace, data path, perf, multiprobes, struct-ops, netfilter, classifier, uprobes, netkit and socket-map to multitracing with small explicit integers. Sets start at UNSPEC zero members and end at double-underscore MAX sentinels, with public MAX_BPF_ATTACH_TYPE and MAX_BPF_LINK_TYPE aliasing their sentinels.

BPF_F_ALLOW_OVERRIDE is bit zero for override and BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI is bit one for multi. BPF_F_REPLACE is bit two with neighbors for before and after and identifier and preorder as bits three through six. The attach link marker is self-defined with documentation pointing at bit thirteen, matching the map link bit. Strict and any alignment occupy bits zero and one in the load domain. Test randomization and state frequency occupy bits two and three. Sleepable is bit four. Fragment and device-bound packet markers are bits five and six. Register-invariant testing is bit seven. Kprobe and uprobe return markers each use bit zero in their domains with path descriptor as bit one for uprobes. Netfilter defragmentation and query-effective and test CPU pinning each use bit zero in their domains, with live frames as bit one and checksum-complete as bit two for test runs.

Pseudo markers use one for map descriptor and five for map index, two for map value and six for indexed value, three for type identifier, four for function, one for pseudo call in its field and two for kernel-function call, with address-space cast defining one. Update modes use zero for create-or-update named BPF_ANY and one for create-only named BPF_NOEXIST and two for update-only named BPF_EXIST, plus four for locked access, eight for CPU-selected per-CPU with number upstairs, sixteen for all CPUs. Creation bits zero through nineteen cover no-prealloc, per-CPU LRU, NUMA, syscall and program read-write gates, build-ID stack, zero seed, clone, mmapable, preserve, inner map, link at thirteen, path descriptor, value-type object, token at sixteen, fault-signal, no-convert and ring overwrite. Representatives are BPF_PSEUDO_MAP_FD and BPF_PSEUDO_BTF_ID and BPF_PSEUDO_FUNC.

Statistics taxonomy currently defines only run-time accounting starting at zero. Stack build-identifier status distinguishes empty terminator, valid identifier-plus-offset and fallback to instruction pointer. Build identifiers are twenty bytes. Stack entries pair a signed status with a twenty-byte identifier plus an eight-byte offset-or-pointer overlay. Common attributes carry an aligned 64-bit log pointer plus size and level and true-size words. Object names are bounded at sixteen unsigned characters. Stream selectors use one for standard output and two for standard error. Carriers are bpf_stack_build_id and bpf_common_attr with limit BPF_OBJ_NAME_LEN and size BPF_BUILD_ID_SIZE.

The system-call carrier is a large discriminated record named bpf_attr with per-command views. Creation view carries type and key and value sizes, entry bound, flags, inner descriptor, NUMA node, name, device index, type-format descriptors and identifiers, a 64-bit extra field with per-type meaning, value-type object descriptor, token descriptor and exclusive-access hash pointer plus length. Element view carries map descriptor plus key pointer plus value-or-next-key overlay plus 64-bit flags. Batch view carries input and output batch pointers plus key and value bases plus count inout plus descriptor plus element and command flags. Load view carries program type and instruction count and pointers to instructions and license, logging level and size and buffer, unused version, program flags and name and device index, expected attach type, type-format descriptor, function and line metadata with record sizes and counts, attach target plus descriptor overlay, relocation counts and arrays, true log size out, token descriptor and array-count binding semantics.

Endian from-aliases equal their to counterparts. Exclusive-add aliases the atomic marker. Program run aliases test-run. Cgroup storage names alias their deprecated predecessors including per-CPU. Public attach and link maxima equal their sentinels and register limit equals its sentinel. Map extra low four bits select bloom hash count with zero meaning five. Arena address must sit on a page boundary. Resizable-hash hint must not exceed the smaller of max entries and 65535 with upper half zero. NUMA node applies only when its flag is set. Token descriptors require their token flags. Cgroup walk allows at most one of descriptor and identifier nonzero. Value-type object applies only when its flag is set.

Variable-length keys with zero-length or flexible tails demand explicit length accounting to avoid overruns, especially with differing IPv4 and IPv6 prefix bounds. Short names and caller-sized log buffers can truncate, with true size possibly larger or smaller than input size. Zero seed is test-only and weakens hashing. Per-CPU least-recently-used nodes cannot migrate across lists. Arena faults can be configured to deliver signals instead of populating pages, and pointer conversion can be suppressed, changing fault and address behavior. Ring overwrite changes loss semantics. Path and token descriptor modes reinterpret fields, so mismatched flags misdirect lookups. Exclusive-access hash gating can deny map access. Batch counts are both input and output and must be rechecked.
